lines: Recolours the world into a deep underwater look.
Nudges your camera toward the closest valid target while you hold a sword, rather than snapping to it.
Tuned for looking legitimate: the pull is smoothed and bounded by a field of view, so it assists an aim you are already making.
Plays an animation you pick, at a speed you pick.
Keeps you in the game rather than being kicked for inactivity.
Disables the game's local detection hooks and rejects abrupt position corrections sent by the server.
Moves your hitbox away from your body when a hit or projectile is about to land, so the damage misses.
Blatant by nature - the desync is visible to anyone watching your position.
Dodges melee and projectiles like AntiDeath, with control over where the safe hitbox is parked and how long it stays there.
Stops other players hiding themselves from you with invisibility animations.
Puts a solid part where the kill plane is, so you land on it instead of falling through.
Undoes the server rubber-banding you back onto an older position.
Recognises a rewind from any direction by keeping a short trail of positions you really held, and holds the correction for a window so the whole multi-frame pull is undone.
Stops a lasso pulling you, and returns you to where you were when it lets go.
Recognises the lasso by the constraint the game builds on your character, so it does not depend on a tag the game may rename.
Stops you being knocked into a ragdoll state.
Lets your shots pass through riot shields.
Pushes you out of a block you are stuck inside before it suffocates you.
Stops tazers immobilising you.
Stops you dying to the void by catching you before you fall past the point of no return.
Offers several recovery methods, from a solid barrier to a block or pearl clutch.
Highlights the armour other players are wearing so you can read their tier at a glance.
Takes your armour off and puts it back on when toggled, for baiting.
Adds trims to your armour.
Draws arrows at the edge of the screen pointing at entities outside your field of view.
Adds and configures the world's lighting objects.
Draws an aura effect around your character.
Draws an aurora across the sky.
Spends frost crystals on the frosty hammer as soon as the next tier is affordable.
Handcuffs nearby entities automatically.
Inflates a balloon the moment you fall into the void.
Banks your resources for you, with a readout of what you are carrying.
Drains the batteries you walk over.
Collects the bees around you and deposits them into your own hives.
Unblocks and blocks again just before each of your hits, so you keep the block up between them.
Aims the block you kick at whoever it can actually hit.
Fortifies the blocks you place with the builder hammer.
Towers straight up while you hold jump, filling the block cell beneath your feet as you rise.
Each cell is only filled once your feet have cleared its top face, so blocks land where you can stand on them.
Buys from the shop as you walk up to it - armour, sword, tools, bow and team upgrades.
Buy Arrows restocks arrows whenever a bow or crossbow is in your inventory and you drop below the Minimum arrows slider.
Takes the blood assassin contract on whoever is worth killing.
Clicks for you while the attack button is held, at a randomised rate between your two CPS bounds.
The randomisation is what keeps the click pattern from reading as machine-driven.
Widens the touch region on Cobalt's batteries so you collect them the moment you are near.
Completes the computer skill check for you.
Heals you automatically once health or shield falls below your threshold.
Counters an opponent's placement or break as it happens.
Places your own TNT on top of an opponent's the moment theirs appears.
Uses the Cyber kit's abilities as they become available.
Breaks the cannon, jumps the moment it launches you, or both.
Detonates your explosives for you.
Collects what your drills produce and attacks with them.
Eats healing items for you.
Collects the eldertree orbs that appear around you.
Releases the infernal saber charge whenever somebody is in range.
Harvests Cletus's crops as soon as they are ready.
Fishes for you.
Wins the fishing minigame the moment it opens.
Opens lucky crates for you.
Breaks the launch pad behind you and jumps off it the moment it fires.
Collects the souls the Grim Reaper drops around you.
Executes marked players as soon as one comes into range.
Heals damage with consumables automatically.
Repairs the Tinker machine whenever the self repair ability is up and you are not mid-swing.
Honors two players when you are finally killed or when the match ends.
Keeps your hotbar arranged the way you set it as items come and go.
Collects the souls the jailor drops.
Uses Kaida's abilities as they come up.
Punches the dragon slayer emblems that land around you.
Uses your kit's abilities for you as they come off cooldown.
Freezes attackers while you are stood on an enemy bed defence.
Puts the scepter of light on the player you picked, every time it comes up.
Throws a lasso at players who come into range and angle.
Electrifies your jellyfish as soon as somebody walks near one.
Fires the cactus wild growth whenever somebody is in range.
Plays the guitar at whoever is hurt and nearest.
Digs up the buried metal the detector finds.
Mines the petrified players the miner leaves behind.
Keeps each of your slimes following the player you picked for it.
Uses midnight the moment you land a melee hit on somebody.
Throws a pearl onto nearby ground once you have fallen a set distance.
Pickpockets everybody in range.
Picks up items that are close to you.
Banks your candy into your pinata whenever you walk past it.
Queues you for another match once the current one ends, or once you are finally killed.
Only the party leader may queue, so it checks that first, and sends the request again if the one made on the match-end frame was swallowed.
Pops the tyres of vehicles around you automatically.
Punches whoever is in front of you, continuously.
Buys the next flamethrower upgrade as soon as it is affordable.
Queues a match from the lobby on its own, which is what lets AutoWin keep playing.
Triggers Berserker Rage the moment you are near an enemy bed.
Throws the airbender tornado at whoever comes into range.
Rejoins a fresh server on its own after a disconnect or a kick.
Releases a charging projectile once it reaches the draw percentage you set.
Reloads the moment you run out of bullets.
Resets your character automatically once you become a criminal.
Respawns you as soon as you die.
Tames the sheep that wander into range.
Fires the projectiles you list between sword swings, switching to them and back.
With Target check off it shoots along your camera direction; with it on it solves the arc onto a target in front of you.
Uses the spirits Evelynn leaves on the players she kills.
Collects the stars that drop around you.
Takes items out of a nearby container automatically.
Places blocks around entities caught in a confined space, to suffocate them.
Sells the chicken while you are at a shop and it is going for what you asked.
Tazes entities around you as they come into range.
Switches to the right tool for whatever you are about to break.
Sends chat messages of your choosing on kills, deaths, bed breaks and wins.
Troll mode replies to anyone who calls you a cheater in chat.
Throws summoned spirits at the emeralds and diamonds around you.
Charges the bow fully on the spot and keeps triple shot armed.
Breathes on whoever is in front of you in dragon form, and doubles your speed off every wing flap.
Drops your resources once you fall past the map, so an enemy cannot collect them from your body.
Owl check and Pearl check both hold the loot: the second walks a telepearl you threw forward and keeps your resources if it would land on ground.
Keeps the warlock staff linked to whoever is nearest.
Spends the owl's lift and heal on whoever it is following.
Plays the match to a win on its own, and keeps going into the next one.
Casts whichever wizard spell you are holding at whoever is in range.
Casts the staff's abilities at whoever is nearby.
Lags the targets around you at chosen moments, which widens the window in which your hits land.
Bypasses the anticheat through the balloon controller.
Warns you when an enemy comes near your bed.
Helps you break a bed - selects the tool, lines up the block and keeps swinging.
Replaces the effect played when a bed is broken.
Draws beds through walls.
Draws the blocks stacked over a bed so you can see what is protecting it.
Rebuilds the defence around your own bed as it is broken.
Draws hives through walls, with their state.
Holds your outgoing packets until you turn it off, then releases them all at once.
Walls you in with blocks on all sides at a keypress.
Recolours the overlay drawn on the block you are pointing at.
Adds soft bloom so bright surfaces glow, and can make generators and ore drops glow too.
Adds upward velocity while jump is held, spread over the climb so no single frame looks like a jump-height violation.
Smoothly steers your aim onto the trajectory that would land a projectile on the target.
Solves the arc for the projectile you are actually holding, so drop and travel time are accounted for.
requires: A bow, crossbow or other projectile source

lines: Leaves a visible trail behind your character.
Breaks the blocks around a target automatically.
Replaces the tracers drawn behind projectiles.
Draws every placed C4 through walls.
Puts a cape on your character.
Renders players through walls in a colour of your choosing.
Changes the colour your name appears in chat.
Moves the chat window where you want it. Works with the legacy chat and with TextChatService.
Types in chat repeatedly on its own.
Flags likely cheaters, grouped into impossible hits, blatant modules, AutoKit, crashers, breaker, and projectile aimbot.
Reads behaviour only - position, timing and replicated state. It never looks at what anybody is running, so there is no module name or signature for a cheat to change.
Every detection needs several impossible readings before it flags, and discards readings taken on a poor connection or explained by a status effect, teleport or knockback.
Every toggle takes effect while the module is running, and all of the position checks share one pass over the players every tenth of a second.
[TEST] Detect self runs the same checks against you, on your behaviour alone, so you can turn a cheat on and watch whether the check meant to catch it fires.
Takes the contents of chests near you.
Retints the world's ambient lighting to a cool teal.
Puts a china hat on your character.
Removes the Zephyr status indicator from your screen.
Shows your local time on screen.
Shows the computers nearby that have not been completed.
Shows your position on screen.
Makes every hit register as a critical.
Replaces the first person crosshair with an image of your choosing.
Replaces your mouse cursor with an image of your choosing.
Gives you a clan tag in chat. Only you can see it.
Gives you a small speed increase for a moment after you take damage.
Changes how damage numbers are drawn.
Aims Davey's cannon for you.
Stops your real position being replicated to other players, so they see you somewhere you are not.
Reports a different device to the server than the one you are on.
Blocks the property-changed detections the game uses to watch your movement.
Changes the name and appearance you show to other players.
Needs an executor function that not every executor provides.
requires: An executor with the required function

lines: Watches how everybody in the match is playing and rates them, which other modules can then sort targets by.
Draws boxes on players, through walls, with the detail you choose.
Withholds your position from the server in bursts, so other players see you where you were rather than where you are.
Shortens the cooldown between block hits so blocks come apart faster.
Shortens how long an item takes to consume.
Drops the item in your hand repeatedly while you hold Q, H or Backspace.
Changes how quickly you interact with things.
Shortens the delay between block placements.
Edits Roblox fast flags from in game.
Needs an executor function that not every executor provides.
requires: An executor with the required function

lines: Tells you what everybody else pulls out of the water.
Flies by driving your character's position and velocity every frame.
Includes a TP Down option that briefly touches the ground so the server keeps seeing you land.
Marks bullets you fire as headshots so they carry headshot damage.
Adjusts the camera's field of view.
Shows your framerate.
Raises the framerate by turning off effects you can spare.
A cinematic camera you fly yourself - smoothing, field of view, roll, depth of field, motion blur, shake, orbit, dolly and keyframed moves.
Hide HUD hides the game interface but leaves the AetherV2 menu up, so you can always get back out of the shot.
Lights the whole world evenly so nothing is hidden in shadow.
Cycles the GUI and module colours through the spectrum.
Draws generators through walls, with their tier and countdown.
Moves your hitbox off your body so damage misses it, while your own hits carry on as normal.
Teleport mode instead cycles you through the air while your health is critical, holding each landing long enough for the fall to resolve.
Changes how fast you fall.
Draws grenades in flight and on the ground.
Teleports the throwables you release to land next to enemy players.
Corrects the Grim Reaper's height so the character is not left too tall.
Alters the firearm you are holding - fire rate, spread, recoil and the rest.
Gives your character the headless look without owning it.
Shows your health in the middle of the screen.
Raises how high a single jump takes you.
Expands the region a sword swing is allowed to resolve against, so hits land on a wider box than the body.
Changes the colour flashed on something you hit.
Points the game at the correct raycast function so hits register where they should.
Plays a sound of your choosing when you land a hit.
Holds a kit ability open, but only for as long as the character still reports it as active.
The 'only while active' part is deliberate: re-asserting an ability the game has ended is what locks a character server-side.
Keeps you alive over the void by withholding replication, dropping to real ground long enough for the landing to register, then returning.
Does not combine with FakeLag - both fight over the same replication window.
Lets you jump again in mid-air, without limit.
TP Down briefly touches the ground and returns you to your height once you have been airborne too long, so the server keeps seeing you land. It does not affect jumping.
Keeps your momentum at maximum permanently.
Gives the car you are driving unlimited boost.
Keeps you riding the elk without it ending.
Stops your stamina draining, so you can sprint indefinitely.
Completes proximity prompt actions instantly instead of holding them.
Sends the hits needed to take a target down in as short a window as the server will accept.
Lets you interact with things further away than the game allows.
Customises the BedWars interface.
Hides the mouse cursor.
Removes the movement slow applied while using an item.
A full visual rewrite - realistic materials, cinematic lighting, weather, ambience and four themed seasons. Changes nothing about gameplay.
Tags dropped items so you can see what is on the floor and where.
Keeps you sprinting while a speed potion is active, which the game would otherwise stop.
Lets you walk through most doors without their key.
Draws your movement keys on screen as you press them.
Attacks entities around you automatically, without aiming at them.
Attack Mode decides who gets the swing: Single stays on one target until they are gone, Switch passes each swing to the next.
Replaces the effect played on a final kill.
Rewrites killfeed messages locally - names, weapon, wording - without removing them.
Tells you who killed you.
Plays a sound of your choosing when you get a kill.
Shows which kit every other player picked.
Draws kit-related objects through walls.
Holds incoming knockback packets back so the push lands later than the hit.
Removes Krystal lagbacks by keeping momentum maxed and muting the correction listeners.
Turns off ragdoll handling and fall damage.
Restores Roblox's older animation blending.
Launches you a long way in your movement direction on jump.
Gets a long jump past the checks that would otherwise reject it.
Draws iron, emeralds and diamonds through walls.
Shows how much memory Roblox is using.
Spawns a missile and teleports it onto a player near your mouse.
Adds motion blur as the camera moves.
Teleports you to whatever position you have selected with the mouse.
Plays your own audio in game, with a playlist, looping and an on-screen player you can drag.
How much further than normal the ability carries you. 1x is the game's own distance.
Teams you with the right people automatically, worked out from the Roblox tools everybody has equipped.
Draws nametags on entities through walls.
Changes the nametag you display to other players.
Removes the client's cap on how often a sword swing may be sent.
Only lifts the local rate limit - the server still resolves each hit on its own terms.
Lets you pass through walls. Hold shift to use NoClip in place of Spider.
Sends every sword activation as it happens rather than waiting for the client's swing cooldown.
Prevents fall damage, by clutching a block or by telling the server you landed safely.
Cancels the fall damage the server would apply when you land.
Removes the camera flash when you take damage.
Removes the delay the game puts between jumps.
Removes the movement slow applied while using an item.
Removes the movement slow the game applies while you are using an item.
Restores the original 4v4v4v4 presentation.
The original nametag, with rank icon and winstreak. Lobby only.
Sends the owl at whoever comes into range on its own.
Turns off every enabled module at once. Needs a second activation, so it cannot fire by accident.
Jumps for you the moment you reach the edge of what you are standing on.
Lets you clip through walls.
Lets your hammer swing through walls to reach what is behind them.
Lets your mining raycasts pass through other players so a body cannot block a break.
Picks items up from further away than the game allows.
Shows your connection time to the server.
Locks your position onto the nearest target so you move wherever they move.
Replaces player models with a mesh of your choosing.
Outlines every player so they read clearly against the map.
Strips the world down to the cheapest possible rendering for framerate.
Lists the effects currently on you.
Redirects the projectiles you launch onto a target, solving the full arc including their movement.
Hooks the game's own launch path, so the shot animates and sounds exactly as a normal one does.
Fires projectiles at entities around you on its own, without you aiming or clicking.
Steps your character out of the path of incoming projectiles once one is judged to be aimed at you.
Marks where a projectile will land - both the ones in the air and the one you are aiming - and highlights anyone the shot would hit.
The aiming marker takes speed and gravity from the game's own launch calculation but always aims along your current cursor, so it tracks the aim rather than lagging behind it.
Draws the arc of projectiles in flight.
Changes how long a proximity prompt has to be held.
Spawns a raven and teleports it onto a player near your mouse.
Extends how far you can attack, place and break.
Distance is applied to the checks the client makes before it sends an action, so every extended action still has to pass the server.
Shows how far away your last hit landed.
Rejoins the server you are already in.
Replaces neon materials so nothing glows.
Removes the level numbers from the player list.
Stops the beast being able to hook onto survivors.
Stops you walking off the edge of a part.
Lays blocks under you as you walk, so you bridge without placing anything yourself.
Fills the ground actually crossed between passes as well as looking ahead, so nothing is skipped at speed.
Saves a building you have placed and lets you lay it back down elsewhere.
Boxes any part whose name you add to the Search list.
Teleports you into a different server.
Replaces the world's lighting with a configurable look.
Removes shadows from the world.
Buys repeatedly while you hold the mouse on a shop item, instead of one purchase per click.
Redirects projectiles you fire onto the target, so you can shoot anywhere and still hit.
Rewrites the shot at the launch remote, so your aim never visibly moves.
Attacks entities around you without moving your camera onto them.
The swing is sent server-side at the target while your view stays where you left it.
Reskins the items you hold and the sounds they make. Only you can see it.
Forces the beast to move at a reduced speed.
A built-in music player.
Replaces in-game sounds with your own.
Forces the beast to use its abilities repeatedly.
Moves you faster than the game allows, by several methods.
CFrame drives your position directly; Bedwars raises the game's own sprint speed. Wall check slides you along surfaces instead of into them.
Shows how fast you are moving, in studs per second.
Lets you climb straight up walls by holding into them.
Spins your character on the spot. Has no visible effect in first person.
Holds your sprint on permanently, including in situations the game would normally stop it.
Warns you when somebody in the server holds a staff rank.
Reports a humanoid state to the server other than the one you are actually in.
Shows what is inside chests without opening them.
Turns the weather to a heavy storm - atmosphere, fog, depth and a cold cinematic grade.
Reveals players hidden behind streamer or disguise mode, and strips the disguised name locally.
Lets you swim through the air as though it were water.
Circles the target automatically while you fight them, holding a set distance.
Steers the blocks Terra throws onto a target, without moving your aim.
Applies a texture pack to the world.
Moves the camera out to third person.
Locks the world clock so the match stays at a time of day you can see in.
Changes how fast the game simulates, so everything you do resolves faster or slower.
Teleports to each target in turn to hit them, then returns, so you can attack people out of reach.
Draws a line from you to each player.
Stops snap traps triggering on you.
Draws traps placed by other teams through walls.
Swings the moment your crosshair passes over an entity, instead of you clicking.
Projectile mode does the same for the projectile in your hand, solving the arc onto whatever you are pointing at.
Throws Triton's harpoon onto nearby ground once you have fallen far enough.
Tidies the kit and main menu interfaces.
Flies the vehicle you are driving.
Raises the top speed of the vehicle you are driving.
Lets your shots pass through vehicles.
Reduces the knockback you take from hits, by a configurable proportion on each axis.
Sends the knockback you receive off in a direction you choose rather than only reducing it.
Changes the animations played on the item in your hands.
Changes how the item in your hands is drawn - position, scale, rotation and sway.
Turns your camera onto opponents automatically.
Helps you land Vulcan's abilities on whoever is in range.
Fills the void with water, sitting at the height AntiFall uses for its barrier.
Marks positions you save with a visible indicator.
Picks the win effect you see. Client-side only.
Changes the winstreak shown next to your name. Only you can see it.
Draws the parts you whitelist through walls and hides the rest.
Raises the maximum camera zoom distance.
